distinguishing_features: Compliant low-modulus polyurethane insert at the flash contact zone (a hardware geometry change), not a procedural/control restriction using existing instrumentation
Absorbs impact stress via elastic deformation of a compliant layer rather than capping a thermal-load/ablation integral
Targets peak contact pressure / abrasion-erosion at a die-flash interface rather than tip erosion from high-enthalpy mass flow
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce peak contact pressure and abrasive-erosive wear at the flash contact zone of a die under cyclic hot-billet impact.
parsed.viable_reason: A low-modulus polyurethane insert deforming under impact pressure to lower peak contact stress is physically sound and testable with the stated wear-depth protocol at the stated scale.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Using a soft compliant layer to spread impact load and reduce contact pressure is a well-known routine engineering expedient, so the distinguishing mechanism is an obvious step rather than a non-obvious departure.
